question.worked_solution:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

- For $x(t)=\operatorname{tan}⁡t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & ={sec}^{2}⁡t \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =2{sec}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t)=\operatorname{sec}⁡t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ {y}^{″}(t) & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t{tan}^{2}⁡t+{sec}^{3}⁡t \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t({tan}^{2}⁡t+{sec}^{2}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨{x}^{″}(t),\,{y}^{″}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{sec}^{2}⁡t\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sec}⁡t({tan}^{2}⁡t+{sec}^{2}⁡t)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
